column1: Glass, in one form or another, has long been in noble service to humans.
column2: 玻璃以某种形式存在，长期以来一直为人类服务。

column1: As one of the most widely used of manufactured materials, and certainly the most versatile, it can be as imposing as a telescope mirror the width of a tennis court or as small and simple as a marble rolling across dirt.
column2: 作为一种被广泛使用的人造材料，它无疑具有极高的多功能性。它可以像网球场那么宽的望远镜镜面那样雄伟壮观，也可以像一颗在泥土上滚动的弹珠那样小巧简洁。

column1: The uses of this adaptable material have been broadened dramatically by new technologies: glass fibre optics — more than eight million miles — carrying telephone and television signals across nations, glass ceramics serving as the nose cones of missiles and as crowns for teeth; tiny glass beads taking radiation doses inside the body to specific organs, even a new type of glass fashioned of nuclear waste in order to dispose of that unwanted material.
column2: 这种可塑性强的材料的用途因新技术而得到了极大的扩展：玻璃纤维光学线路能够传输超过800万英里的电话和电视信号；玻璃陶瓷则被用作导弹的鼻锥或牙齿修复材料；微小的玻璃珠可以将辐射剂量传递到体内的特定器官；甚至还有一种由核废料制成的新型玻璃，用于处理那些不再需要的物质。

column1: On the horizon are optical computers.
column2: 在地平线上是光学计算机。

column1: These could store programs and process information by means of light – pulses from tiny lasers – rather than electrons.
column2: 这些装置可以通过光——即微小激光发出的脉冲——而不是电子来存储程序和处理信息。

column1: And the pulses would travel over glass fibres, not copper wire.
column2: 这些脉冲会通过玻璃纤维传播，而不是铜线。

column1: These machines could function hundreds of times faster than today’s electronic computers and hold vastly more information.
column2: 这些机器的运行速度可以比今天的电子计算机快数百倍，并且能够存储海量信息。

column1: Today fibre optics are used to obtain a clearer image of smaller and smaller objects than ever before – even bacterial viruses.
column2: 如今，光纤技术被广泛应用于对越来越小的物体进行清晰成像——甚至包括细菌病毒也是如此。

column1: A new generation of optical instruments is emerging that can provide detailed imaging of the inner workings of cells.
column2: 新一代光学仪器正在出现，这些仪器能够实现对细胞内部运作的详细成像。

column1: It is the surge in fibre optic use and in liquid crystal displays that has set the U.S. glass industry (a 16 billion dollar business employing some 150,000 workers) to building new plants to meet demand.
column2: 正是光纤和液晶显示器使用量的激增，促使美国玻璃业（一个规模达160亿美元、雇用约15万人的行业）新建工厂以满足需求。
column5: liquid crystal displays|n. 液晶显示器

column1: But it is not only in technology and commerce that glass has widened its horizons.
column2: 不过，玻璃的应用范围并不仅限于技术和商业领域。

column1: The use of glass as art, a tradition that spins back at least to Roman times, is also booming.
column2: 将玻璃用于艺术创作的做法已经有着至少罗马时代的传统了，这一趋势如今依然十分流行。

column1: Nearly everywhere, it seems, men and women are blowing glass and creating works of art.
column2: 似乎在几乎每个地方，都有男人和女人在吹玻璃并创作艺术品。

column1: “I didn’t sell a piece of glass until 1975,” Dale Chihuly said, smiling, for in the 18 years since the end of the dry spell, he has become one of the most financially successful artists of the 20th century.
column2: ‘直到1975年，我都没有卖出一块玻璃作品，’戴尔·奇胡利微笑着说。在那段低迷时期之后，他花了18年的时间，成为了20世纪最成功的艺术家之一。

column1: He now has a new commission – a glass sculpture for the headquarters building of a pizza company – for which his fee is half a million dollars.
column2: 现在他获得了一项新的委托任务——为一家披萨公司的总部大楼制作一座玻璃雕塑。他的报酬是五十万美元。

column1: But not all the glass technology that touches our lives is ultra-modern.
column2: 但并非所有影响我们生活的玻璃技术都是超现代的。

column1: Consider the simple light bulb; at the turn of the century most light bulbs were hand blown, and the cost of one was equivalent to half a day’s pay for the average worker.
column2: 以简单的灯泡为例：在世纪之交时，大多数灯泡都是手工制造的，其价格相当于普通工人半天工资的价值。

column1: In effect, the invention of the ribbon machine by Corning in the 1920s lighted a nation.
column2: 实际上，康宁公司在20世纪20年代发明的带状材料加工设备，为整个国家带来了巨大的变革。

column1: The price of a bulb plunged.
column2: 灯泡的价格暴跌。

column1: Small wonder that the machine has been called one of the great mechanical achievements of all time.
column2: 难怪这台机器被称作人类历史上最伟大的机械成就之一。

column1: Yet it is very simple: a narrow ribbon of molten glass travels over a moving belt of steel in which there are holes.
column2: 然而它非常简单：一条狭窄的熔融玻璃带在带有孔洞的移动钢带上行进。

column1: The glass sags through the holes and into waiting moulds.
column2: 玻璃通过孔洞流入等待中的模具中。

column1: Puffs of compressed air then shape the glass.
column2: 然后，通过压缩空气的作用来塑造玻璃的形状。

column1: In this way, the envelope of a light bulb is made by a single machine at the rate of 66,000 an hour, as compared with 1,200 a day produced by a team of four glassblowers.
column2: 通过这种方式，一个灯泡的封装工作可以在一台机器上以每小时66,000个的速度完成，而相比之下，由四名玻璃吹制工组成的团队每天只能生产1,200个这样的灯泡。

column1: The secret of the versatility of glass lies in its interior structure.
column2: 玻璃多用途的秘诀在于其内部结构。

column1: Although it is rigid, and thus like a solid, the atoms are arranged in a random disordered fashion, characteristic of a liquid.
column2: 虽然这种物质具有刚性，看起来像固体一样，但实际上其原子是以一种随机无序的方式排列的，这正是液体的特征。

column1: In the melting process, the atoms in the raw materials are disturbed from their normal position in the molecular structure; before they can find their way back to crystalline arrangements the glass cools.
column2: 在熔化过程中，原材料中的原子会从分子结构中的正常位置被扰动；在它们能够重新恢复到晶态排列之前，玻璃就会冷却下来。

column1: This looseness in molecular structure gives the material what engineers call tremendous “formability” which allows technicians to tailor glass to whatever they need.
column2: 分子结构的松散性赋予了这种材料工程师所称的“极佳可成形性”，使技术人员能够根据需要将其定制成各种形状。

column1: Today, scientists continue to experiment with new glass mixtures and building designers test their imaginations with applications of special types of glass.
column2: 如今，科学家们持续实验新型玻璃混合物，建筑设计师则通过特殊类型玻璃的应用发挥其想象力。

column1: A London architect, Mike Davies, sees even more dramatic buildings using molecular chemistry.
column2: 伦敦建筑师迈克·戴维斯认为，未来建筑可以借助分子化学实现更戏剧性的表现。

column1: “Glass is the great building material of the future, the ‘dynamic skin’,” he said.
column2: “玻璃是未来的伟大建筑材料，堪称‘动态皮肤’。”他说。

column1: “Think of glass that has been treated to react to electric currents going through it, glass that will change from clear to opaque at the push of a button, that gives you instant curtains.
column2: 设想一种经过处理能对电流作出反应的玻璃，只需按一下按钮，它就能从透明变为不透明，瞬间变成窗帘。

column1: Think of how the tall buildings in New York could perform a symphony of colours as the glass in them is made to change colours instantly.”
column2: 想想纽约那些高楼如何通过玻璃瞬间变色，上演一场色彩交响乐。

column1: Glass as instant curtains is available now, but the cost is exorbitant.
column2: 现在已有可即时转化为窗帘的玻璃产品，但价格极为昂贵。

column1: As for the glass changing colours instantly, that may come true.
column2: 至于玻璃能瞬间变色这一点，也许真的会实现。

column1: Mike Davies’s vision may indeed be on the way to fulfilment.
column2: 迈克·戴维斯的愿景确实有可能实现。
